Check the health of the rb3 cache

Source: R/doctor.R
rb3_doctor.Rd

rb3_doctor() checks the download records (meta.sqlite) and the raw files of the cache, and finds the gaps in the time series of a template's dataset layer: business days in a period that have no rows. It only reports; it never changes the cache.

Usage

rb3_doctor(
  template = NULL,
  layer = "input",
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  calendar = NULL
)

Arguments

template

A template id (see list_templates()). NULL (default) runs only the health checks, for the whole cache.

layer

The dataset layer to check for gaps: "input" (default) or "staging".

from, to

The period to check (Date or "YYYY-MM-DD"). Defaults: the first and the last refdate in the layer. Use to = Sys.Date() to also find recent dates not fetched yet.

calendar

A bizdays calendar name. NULL (default) uses the template's calendar (the calendar field of its YAML file). Templates without a calendar need this argument. A value passed here overrides the template's calendar.

Value

Invisibly, a tibble with one row per finding and the columns template, layer, check ("gap", "stale_meta", "missing_raw" or "orphan_raw"), refdate (the missing date of a gap), reason (for gaps, see Details) and detail (the record's download arguments, or the raw file name). A healthy cache gives 0 rows.

Details

Health checks (always; for one template when template is given):

  • stale_meta: records whose download arguments differ from the template's current arguments, or whose template no longer exists. For example, records of b3-reference-rates created before rb3 0.1.1 still have a curve_name argument. They are never used again.

  • missing_raw: records marked as downloaded whose raw file does not exist.

  • orphan_raw: files in the raw/ folder that no record uses (only when template = NULL).

Gap check (only with template): the business days of the period with no rows in the layer. Each missing date gets a reason, taken from the download records:

  • never_fetched: no record for this date (or year). Fetch it with fetch_marketdata().

  • download_failed: the download failed, or B3 sent an empty file. Fetch it again; B3 may not have the file.

  • not_read: the file was downloaded but not read. Use fetch_marketdata(..., reprocess = TRUE).

  • no_data: the file was read but had no usable data.

A day the exchange was closed, although the calendar says it was open, shows as no_data or as download_failed, depending on what B3 sends for that template on a closed day.

  • not_in_layer: the record says the file was read, but the layer has no rows for that date. Either the layer and the records disagree (a deleted dataset folder, a staging layer not rebuilt: use reprocess = TRUE), or the file held another date than the one requested. For yearly templates it means that the year's file has no data for that day.

When several records cover one date (yearly templates, or templates with an extra argument such as index), the best status wins: ok, then no data, then not read, then download failed. Templates without a refdate or year argument (snapshots such as b3-indexes-composition) have no time series, and the gap check is skipped. A date counts as present if it has any row, even if only one index or one curve has it.

Calendar

The expected dates are bizdays::bizseq(from, to, calendar). A period outside the calendar's range is an error that shows the calendar's last date: update bizdays or pass a shorter to.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# health of the whole cache
rb3_doctor()
# gaps in the input layer of the yield curves
res <- rb3_doctor("b3-reference-rates")
# check up to today, to see the recent dates not fetched yet
rb3_doctor("b3-futures-settlement-prices", to = Sys.Date())
# fetch the dates that were never fetched
dates <- res |> dplyr::filter(reason == "never_fetched") |> dplyr::pull(refdate)
fetch_marketdata("b3-reference-rates", refdate = dates)
} # }
